project.name: Sphere topology
project.description: Reusable Lean topology and singular homology: fixed points of complex-valued continuous maps on closed balls of nonnegative radius whose sphere-boundary images lie in the ball, with no interior image bound; degree-zero boundary restrictions and non-retraction for the complex closed unit disk; arbitrary-index circle bouquets, inclusions, positive-generator homomorphisms, retractions and generator nonidentity, and a positive-generator-preserving free-group identification with the universal property for group targets in independent universes; jointly injective factor retractions and factorwise T0/T1/T2 classification for arbitrary chosen-point wide pushouts, including empty families; normalization of nowhere-zero continuous fields, identity-to-antipodal homotopies from orthogonal fields, integral subdivision, cover-small chains and two-open Mayer-Vietoris, nonnegative reduced integral homology and degree-zero criteria for path connectedness. Finite-fiber coverings give transfers on all-simplex singular chains and ordinary homology with categorical coefficient objects. Signed-period circle fundamental-group coordinates, generic based lifting, monodromy, maps of covers and deck-group comparisons are supplied by Fundamental Groupoids, their canonical home, and re-exported through deprecated Sphere circle and covering module paths. H-space loop multiplication, circle degree, free homotopy and disk results remain in Sphere; private coordinate and circle H-space checks are in SphereTopologyTest.CircleHSpace. Explicit circle and two-sphere calculations give the antipodal action on H2 of the standard two-sphere and its continuous orthogonal-field hairy-ball theorem. The metric two-sphere lifted to any universe has a non-nullhomotopic identity, distinct identity and north-constant based homotopy classes, and a nontrivial second homotopy group.

methods.tool_setup: Lean and Lake with pinned mathlib APIs, compiler feedback and Lean tactics.

automation.notes: Project code, proofs, documentation and metadata are AI-authored. See docs/CREDITS.md for contributor and source-origin attribution. AI authorship does not establish correctness, ownership or redistribution rights; third-party implementation and source assets are not redistributed here.

sources.title: The K-book: An Introduction to Algebraic K-theory
A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology
sources.location: Revised edition, Chapter 1, §§5–7; Chapter 2, §8; Chapter 8, §§1–2, pp. 57–58; Chapter 9, §1, p. 65; Chapter 16, Problem 3.

highlights.title: Brouwer fixed points on complex disks
highlights.statement: For c : ℂ and r ≥ 0, every continuous complex-valued map on Metric.closedBall c r has a fixed point if it maps the sphere boundary into that ball, without any interior image bound.

highlights.title: Hairy-ball theorem for the metric two-sphere
highlights.statement: Every continuous map V from the unit sphere in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) satisfying ⟨p, V(p)⟩ = 0 at every sphere point p vanishes somewhere.

highlights.title: Free fundamental groups of circle bouquets
highlights.statement: For any label type I and independent ambient and label universes, FreeGroup I is multiplicatively equivalent to the fundamental group of the point-wide-pushout CircleBouquet.space I at its common point, sending each free generator to its included counterclockwise complex-unit-circle loop, including for empty I.

highlights.title: Sphere cogroups and sharp cocommutativity
highlights.statement: For every n : ℕ and universe u, Metric.Sphere.cogroup n gives the last-axis-north-based ULift.{u} of the unit sphere in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)) a group-object structure in the ordinary opposite based-homotopy category, whose specified ordered-pinch monoid structure is commutative exactly when 0 < n.

highlights.title: Nontrivial second homotopy group of the metric two-sphere
highlights.statement: In every universe u, the second homotopy group of Metric.Sphere.basedSpace.{u} 1, the last-axis-north-based ULift.{u} of the unit sphere in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), is nontrivial.

headlines.title: H-space fundamental groups commute
headlines.text:
**H-space fundamental groups commute.**
[`FundamentalGroup.mul_comm`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HSpaceFundamentalGroup.lean)
applies at the unit of any H-space, using only its two relative unit
homotopies. No associativity, commutativity or strict unit laws for the
multiplication are assumed. Continuous multiplication with a strict unit
also gives `Path.mul_homotopic_trans`, without associativity or inverses.

headlines.title: Normalized circle fundamental groups and degree
headlines.text:
**Normalized circle fundamental groups and degree.** For real `T ≠ 0`,
[`AddCircle.fundamentalGroupEquivInt`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/fundamental-groupoids/blob/main/FundamentalGroupoids/AlgebraicTopology/FundamentalGroup/Circle.lean)
is supplied by Fundamental Groupoids and identifies `π₁(AddCircle T, 0)`
with `Multiplicative ℤ`, including signed periods, lifted endpoints and
agreement with the complex unit circle.
[`Circle.degree`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/CircleDegree.lean) classifies free
homotopy of arbitrary continuous circle self-maps. Composition multiplies
degree, while pointwise multiplication adds it, including multiset products
with repeated factors. The map `z ↦ z^n` has degree `n : ℤ`, and degree different
from `1` is a sufficient, not necessary, fixed-point condition. No based-map
premise is needed.

headlines.title: Disk boundary degree and non-retraction
headlines.text:
**Disk boundary degree and non-retraction.** Every continuous map
`G : C(Metric.closedBall (0 : ℂ) 1, Circle)` has boundary restriction of
degree zero, so that restriction is not the identity on `Circle`
([`Disk`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/Disk.lean)). The boundary map is the
coordinate-preserving inclusion of the complex unit circle into the closed
unit disk; no basedness premise is imposed. This is not a theorem about
arbitrary-dimensional disks or an extension converse.

headlines.title: Forward intersections with spheres
headlines.text:
**Forward intersections with spheres.** In a real inner-product affine space,
[`Sphere.rayInter`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/ForwardRay.lean) continues from
`q` through a distinct closed-ball point `x` to the sphere, with parameter
at least one even when `q` is outside the ball. For a closed-ball start,
positive sphere-intersection parameters are characterized by the upper root,
and a boundary second point is fixed, including the diagonal. The total
parameter and point formulas are jointly continuous on the whole off-diagonal;
boundary starts agree with Mathlib's `Sphere.secondInter` when `x` is in the
closed ball. No finite-dimensionality, completeness or global radius-sign
assumption is needed.

headlines.title: Continuous ray maps and boundary-only strict retractions
headlines.text:
**Continuous ray maps and boundary-only strict retractions.** In a real
inner-product affine torsor,
[`Sphere.rayInterMap`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/ForwardRayMap.lean) turns an
ambient-valued continuous map `f` on a closed ball, with `f x ≠ x` at every
point, into a continuous map to its sphere. If boundary points have images
in the closed ball, composition with the boundary inclusion is exactly the
identity. No image condition is imposed on interior points; a fixed-point-free
continuous closed-ball selfmap is a specialization.
Vector and point universes are independent, and radii are arbitrary real
numbers, with no finite-dimensionality, completeness or nontriviality premise.
This generalizes the boundary-fixing construction in May's closed-disk
argument (Chapter 1, §6), not a fixed-point theorem in this generality.

headlines.title: Generic stereographic geometry
headlines.text:
**Generic stereographic geometry.** For
`E : Type u` with `[NormedAddCommGroup E]` and `[InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`,
let `S := Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1` be the canonical sphere subtype,
`p q : S`, `H := (ℝ ∙ (p : E))ᗮ` and
`σ := stereographic (norm_eq_of_mem_sphere p)`.
[`stereographicHomeomorph p`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/Stereographic.lean)
identifies `({p}ᶜ : Set S)` with `H`; for `hpq : p ≠ q`,
`stereographicOverlapHomeomorph p q hpq` identifies
`({p}ᶜ ∩ {q}ᶜ : Set S)` with `H \ {σ q}`.
These retain Mathlib's factor-2 stereographic map: the excluded pole is
`+p`, and the one-pole inverse sends `0` to `-p`. The overlap target deletes
zero exactly when `q = -p`.

headlines.title: Last-axis one-point compactification coordinates
headlines.text:
**Last-axis one-point compactification coordinates.**
[`EuclideanSpace.onePointHomeomorphSphere`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/OnePointSphere.lean)
identifies `OnePoint (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))` with the unit sphere in
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+1))`, for every `n`, including zero. Infinity maps
to the last unit vector and finite zero to its antipode. Finite coordinates
have denominator `‖x‖²+4`, and the off-pole inverse has coordinates
`2*p_i/(1-p_last)`. The underlying append-zero-last linear isometry also
applies over `RCLike` scalars; only the sphere homeomorphism is real.

headlines.title: Finite generalized loops and based sphere-map classes
headlines.text:
**Finite generalized loops and based sphere-map classes.** For every `n : ℕ`,
[`GenLoop.sphereHomeomorph`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/Sphere.lean)
gives a homeomorphism from `GenLoop (Fin n) X x` to
`{F : C(Sⁿ, X) // F (EuclideanSpace.northPoint n) = x}`, where `Sⁿ` is the
unit sphere in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+1))`.
`HomotopyGroup.equivSphereClasses` gives a natural set equivalence from
`HomotopyGroup (Fin n) X x` to the existing `ZerothHomotopy` of this subtype.
Inverse representatives precompose with
[`Cube.collapseToSphere`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/CubeSphere.lean).
Constants and based postcomposition are preserved, including between targets
in independent universes. Equality of sphere-map components is exactly
homotopy relative to the singleton last-axis north pole. In dimension one,
`HomotopyGroup.pi1MulEquivFundamentalGroup_sphereHomeomorph` sends the component
associated with a based path to that path's fundamental-group class. Targets
require only a topology and a chosen point, with no separation, local compactness
or well-pointedness hypothesis.

For every `n : ℕ` and arbitrary `X : BasedTopCat.{u}`,
[`HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/SphereHom.lean)
is an ordinary set equivalence from `HomotopyGroup (Fin n) X.right (BasedTopCat.point X)`
to morphisms from the north-based `ULift.{u} Sⁿ` to `X` in the based-homotopy
category. Targets may be any objects of the under category, not only ones
presented by `BasedTopCat.of`, and the construction applies in every universe `u`.
Forward representatives precompose `GenLoop.sphereHomeomorph n` with `ULift.down`;
inverse representatives have values
`t ↦ f.right.hom (ULift.up (Cube.collapseToSphere n t))`.
Here `n = 0` means `S⁰` and `n = 1` means `S¹`. This set comparison alone
specifies no multiplication on the hom-set or group in dimension zero; the
positive-dimensional group comparison below uses a multiplicative opposite.

headlines.title: Positive-dimensional sphere pinch and folding
headlines.text:
**Positive-dimensional sphere pinch and folding.** For `d = n + 1 > 0`,
[`Metric.Sphere.pinch n`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/SpherePinch.lean) maps the
existing last-axis unit sphere `Sᵈ` to its two-factor point-wide-pushout.
Its cube pullback traverses the left factor before the right factor in
coordinate zero; the two closed-half formulas agree at the separating slice,
and fixed quarter-point witnesses give distinct non-head values.
`surjective_pinch` and `isQuotientMap_pinch` show that it is surjective and a
quotient map for the topology of that categorical target. `pinch_eq_head_iff`
identifies its head fiber with the equator where ambient coordinate zero
vanishes; `pinch_eq_pinch_iff` says that two points have the same image exactly
when they are equal or both lie on that equator.
[`Metric.Sphere.pinchFold`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/SpherePinchFold.lean)
is jointly continuous on the ordinary compact-open based-map subtype and
preserves simultaneous paths of its factors, for arbitrary topological targets.
Its identity/constant folds in opposite orders differ at the left quarter-point,
including for the circle.
[`pinch_fold_class`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/SpherePinch.lean)
compares folding based maps `F, G` with the existing homotopy-group
multiplication: writing `J` for the inverse sphere-class comparison, the
result is `J(G) * J(F)`, including in dimension one. Each original factor
retraction composed with the pinch is homotopic to the identity relative to
the north pole. `pinch_fold_homotopicRel_assoc` gives associativity of folding
three arbitrary based maps up to north-pole-relative homotopy for every `d > 0`;
its original three-inclusion specialization, `pinch_homotopicRel_coassoc`,
gives coassociativity into the three-factor point-wide-pushout. The two
iterated maps are not equal: `pinch_coassoc_nondegenerate` exhibits their
different values at the same cube time `3/8`, and three distinct non-head
inclusion values of the left nesting. For `d = n + 2 ≥ 2`,
`pinch_fold_homotopicRel_swap` gives a north-pole-relative homotopy when the
two arbitrary based factor maps are interchanged. Its original-inclusion specialization,
`pinch_homotopicRel_swap`, identifies the pinch up to that relative homotopy
with the original categorical factor swap after the pinch. Raw folding and
based postcomposition allow independently universed targets with only a
topology. No dimension-one cocommutativity, zero-sphere pinch or choice of
sphere orientation is asserted by these geometric comparisons.

headlines.title: Based coordinate reflections and coinverses
headlines.text:
**Based coordinate reflections and coinverses.** For every positive sphere
dimension `d = n + 1`, including S¹, and every pre-last axis `i : Fin (n + 1)`,
[`coordinateReflection`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/SphereCoordinateReflection.lean)
negates exactly ambient coordinate `i.castSucc` and fixes the last-axis north
pole. It is involutive, differs from the identity, and is uniquely determined
by its cube pullback: reversing axis `i` of the original collapse. For an
arbitrary based map to a topological space,
[`coordinateReflection_precomp_class`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/SphereCoordinateReflection.lean)
identifies precomposition by this reflection with the existing homotopy-group
inverse. Folding the pinch with reflection and identity in either order is
homotopic to the north constant relative to the north pole, for every such
axis; neither folded map is equal to that constant. These results do not
require commutativity and do not assert S¹ cocommutativity.

headlines.title: Positive-dimensional spheres as cogroups
headlines.text:
**Positive-dimensional spheres as cogroups.**
[`Metric.Sphere.cogroup`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/SphereCogroup.lean) bundles
the lifted original sphere of dimension `n + 1`, based at the last-axis north
pole, as a stock group object in the ordinary opposite based-homotopy category.
Multiplication, unit and inversion are opposite to the quotient classes of,
respectively, the original pinch with its ordered wedge comparisons, collapse
followed by the head of the empty wedge, and first-coordinate reflection. The five group-object
laws use the original north-relative homotopies and the chosen cartesian
associator. `cogroupGrpObj` and the cartesian structure are named data, not
global instances. Installing them locally gives the stock group on outgoing
based homotopy classes into any based target; its multiplication is pinch
followed by the paired classes. The cogroup construction alone makes no
identification with an existing homotopy group; the separate comparison below
uses a multiplicative opposite. No dimension-one cocommutativity, zero-sphere
cogroup or orientation choice is asserted.

headlines.title: Homotopy groups and the sphere-map group
headlines.text:
**Homotopy groups and the sphere-map group.** For `n : ℕ` and any
`X : BasedTopCat.{u}`,
[`HomotopyGroup.mulOppositeEquivSphereHom`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/SphereCogroup.lean)
gives a multiplicative equivalence from
`(HomotopyGroup (Fin (n + 1)) X.right (BasedTopCat.point X))ᵐᵒᵖ`
to the canonical `CategoryTheory.yonedaGrp` evaluation of `Metric.Sphere.cogroup n`
at `op (op (Q.obj X))`, where `Q := BasedTopCat.homotopyQuotient`.
Its elements are incoming morphisms to the cogroup carrier in the ordinary
opposite based-homotopy category; their unops are outgoing classes from the
lifted, north-based `Sⁿ⁺¹` to `X`. These categorical opposites differ from the source's
multiplicative opposite. Writing `E := HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom (n + 1) X`,
`mulOppositeEquivSphereHom_apply_op` sends `MulOpposite.op a` to `(E a).op`;
`mulOppositeEquivSphereHom_symm_apply` sends `f` to
`MulOpposite.op (E.symm f.unop)`, without inversion or a change of representative.
`mulOppositeEquivSphereHom_naturality` identifies based postcomposition by
`h : X ⟶ Y` with the Yoneda action on `(Q.map h).op.op`.
Since folding `F, G` represents `J(G) * J(F)`, the source opposite matters
even for `n = 0`, which is `S¹`. No direct group comparison by the same class
map without that opposite, S¹ commutativity or group on S⁰ is asserted.
Targets require only their topology and chosen point.

headlines.title: Sharp cocommutativity of sphere cogroups
headlines.text:
**Sharp cocommutativity of sphere cogroups.** For every `n : ℕ` in any universe,
[`Metric.Sphere.cogroup_isCommMonObj_iff`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/SphereCocommutativity.lean)
proves `IsCommMonObj (Metric.Sphere.cogroupCarrier n) ↔ 0 < n`: the specified
sphere cogroup of dimension `n + 1` is commutative exactly in dimensions at least
two. `cogroup_isCommMonObj` gives the positive case using the sphere-map group
comparison and Mathlib's Eckmann–Hilton theorem for every based target.
`cogroup_not_isCommMonObj_zero` excludes the original circle S¹ using this
library's noncommuting positive two-circle bouquet generators and sphere-map
comparison, Mathlib's first-homotopy-group equivalence and its stock
commutativity lemmas. Multiplication remains the original ordered-pinch class.
These are named properties, not global commutativity instances; no group on
S⁰ is asserted.

headlines.title: Nontrivial second homotopy group of S²
headlines.text:
**Nontrivial second homotopy group of S².**
[`Metric.Sphere.id_not_nullhomotopic_two`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HomotopyGroup/SphereNontrivial.lean)
shows that the identity of the unit two-sphere in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`,
lifted to any universe, is not homotopic to any constant map.
`Metric.Sphere.homotopyQuotient_id_ne_const_two` distinguishes its identity
class from the constant class at the last-axis north pole in the based-homotopy
category. `HomotopyGroup.nontrivial_sphere_two` proves that the corresponding
`π₂` is nontrivial. The sphere is `Metric.Sphere.basedSpace 1`; no computation
of the second homotopy group is asserted.

headlines.title: Topology of real normed unit spheres
headlines.text:
**Topology of real normed unit spheres.** The topology-only APIs in
[`Homotopy.Sphere`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/Sphere.lean) are stated for
`E : Type u` with `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]`, using its
original norm and `S := Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1`.
`contractibleSpace_sphere_compl_singleton p` gives
`ContractibleSpace ({p}ᶜ : Set S)` without a rank premise; simple connectivity
follows from Mathlib's `SimplyConnectedSpace.ofContractible`.
`pathConnectedSpace_sphere_compl_poles p q h` gives
`PathConnectedSpace ({p}ᶜ ∩ {q}ᶜ : Set S)` for all `p,q`, including equal
poles, when `h : 2 < Module.rank ℝ E` (cardinal rank).
`simplyConnectedSpace_unitSphere h` gives `SimplyConnectedSpace S` under the
same rank bound, including the usual `Sⁿ` for `n ≥ 2` and infinite-dimensional
spaces. No completeness, finite-dimensionality, supplied pole for the whole
sphere, ambient connectivity or overlap-nonemptiness assumption is needed.
These statements generalize May's finite Euclidean sphere setting; the
orthogonal-coordinate charts above still require an inner product.

headlines.title: Canonical antipodal quotient covering
headlines.text:
**Canonical antipodal quotient covering.** For `E : Type w` with
`[NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]`,
[`Metric.Sphere.isQuotientCoveringMap_toProjectivization`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Geometry/Projectivization.lean)
makes the canonical continuous map
`Metric.Sphere.toProjectivization : C(Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1, Projectivization ℝ E)`
a quotient covering for the scalar action of `Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ) 1`,
whose elements act by identity and negation. The sphere uses the original norm;
the target has the quotient topology from nonzero vectors. No inner product,
dimension, completeness, local compactness, nonemptiness, nontriviality or
freeness hypothesis is required. This includes the zero space's empty-to-empty
map and the two-point-to-one-point map for `E = ℝ`.

headlines.title: Real projective fundamental groups and lifted endpoints
headlines.text:
**Real projective fundamental groups and lifted endpoints.** For a real
normed space `E` with `2 < Module.rank ℝ E`,
[`Projectivization.fundamentalGroupEquivZModTwo`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/Projectivization.lean)
identifies `π₁(Projectivization ℝ E, b)` with `Multiplicative (ZMod 2)`.
A chosen unit lift over the supplied basepoint fixes the lift description,
but not the resulting coordinate. The identity means returning to that lift;
`Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ZMod 2)` means reaching its antipode. The sphere
uses the given norm, with no inner-product, finite-dimensionality or
completeness assumption, including infinite cardinal rank.

headlines.title: Boundary-only fixed points on complex closed balls
headlines.text:
**Boundary-only fixed points on complex closed balls.** A continuous map
`F : C(Metric.closedBall c r, ℂ)`, with `c : ℂ` and `0 ≤ r`, has a fixed
point if its sphere-boundary images lie in that ball
([`Complex.exists_fixedPoint_closedBall_of_boundary_mapsTo`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/Disk.lean)).
No image bound is imposed on interior points, and no ambient extension is
assumed. The continuous self-map case retains the API
[`Complex.exists_fixedPoint_closedBall`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/Disk.lean).
This includes the radius-zero singleton and generalizes May's closed unit
disk self-map theorem (Chapter 1, §6, p. 10); it is not a higher-dimensional
fixed-point theorem.

headlines.title: Quotient presentations of topological wide pushouts (Fundamental Groupoids)
headlines.text:
**Quotient presentations of topological wide pushouts (Fundamental Groupoids).**
[`TopCat.widePushoutHomeomorph`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/fundamental-groupoids/blob/main/FundamentalGroupoids/Topology/Category/TopCat/Limits/WidePushout.lean)
identifies the quotient of `B ⊕ Σ i, X i` by `b ∼ (i, f i b)` with the
categorical wide pushout of arbitrary continuous maps `f i : B ⟶ X i`,
preserving the head and every factor. Continuity and descent have an
independent target universe; empty and singleton families need no separation,
compactness or homotopy assumptions.

headlines.title: Embeddings, closed maps and neighborhoods of point-wide-pushouts
headlines.text:
**Embeddings, closed maps and neighborhoods of point-wide-pushouts.**
[`TopCat.isEmbedding_widePushoutDesc_point`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/OpenEmbedding.lean)
promotes point-preserving component embeddings to an embedding of the
canonical wide pushouts; open or closed component embeddings give an open or
closed embedding, respectively. Point reflection and component open or closed
maps also suffice for the corresponding map property. The index may be
arbitrary or empty, and source and target universes are independent, with no
separation assumptions. The [ULift caller](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/PointLift.lean)
accommodates smaller original factors. For a given function relabeling factors
with finite label fibers, the [closed-map criterion](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/ClosedMap.lean)
assumes closed component maps, point reflection, and the head and factor equations.
The function is closed exactly when each omitted target factor has a closed chosen-point
singleton, with no continuity or separation assumption. Closed rays based at zero give a proper
closed embedding that is not open. For open neighborhoods of the attaching points,
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointNeighborhoodHomeomorph`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/OpenNeighborhood.lean)
identifies their wide pushout with its open range in the ordinary subtype topology.

headlines.title: Parametrized continuity and homotopy gluing (Fundamental Groupoids)
headlines.text:
**Parametrized continuity and homotopy gluing (Fundamental Groupoids).**
[`TopCat.continuous_prod_iff_of_isColimit`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/fundamental-groupoids/blob/main/FundamentalGroupoids/Topology/Category/TopCat/Limits/Products.lean)
checks joint continuity on the legs of any supplied topological colimit under
Mathlib's `LocallyCompactPair P Y` hypothesis; a locally compact parameter
suffices, with no separation condition on the target. Parameter and target
universes are independent. Compatible families on a wide pushout's head and
every factor descend continuously, with computation, uniqueness, fixed-parameter
and reparametrization laws. Compatible interval homotopies glue at all times,
without requiring the common point to stay fixed. Point-relative descent is
supplied by
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointHomotopyRel`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/fundamental-groupoids/blob/main/FundamentalGroupoids/Topology/Homotopy/WidePushout.lean).

headlines.title: Point-relative equivalences and contractions
headlines.text:
**Point-relative equivalences and contractions.**
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointHomotopyEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/PointHomotopyEquiv.lean)
descends point-preserving factor maps and supplied relative inverse homotopies.
Inverse point preservation follows from the forward maps and left relative
homotopies. The chosen relative witnesses compute on the head and every factor.
Supplied contractions fixing the attaching points contract the wide pushout,
including an empty index family. This is stronger data than ordinary factor
contractibility; countably many endpoint-zero intervals give a nontrivial client.

headlines.title: Factor retractions and separation of point-wide-pushouts
headlines.text:
**Factor retractions and separation of point-wide-pushouts.**
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointRetraction`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushoutRetraction.lean)
retracts the categorical wide pushout of arbitrary chosen-point spaces onto
any selected factor, and each factor inclusion is an embedding. The
[retractions jointly distinguish points](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/Separation.lean),
without separation or finiteness assumptions, even for the empty index family.
The pushout is T₀, T₁ or Hausdorff exactly when every factor has that property;
factorwise inheritance is available by instance inference. Index and space
universes are independent. No embedding into the product is asserted.
The circle-bouquet retractions specialize this construction.

headlines.title: Compact subsets meet finitely many pointed factors
headlines.text:
**Compact subsets meet finitely many pointed factors.**
[`finite_widePushoutPointSupport`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/Compactness.lean)
applies to arbitrary indexed T₁ spaces attached at chosen points. A compact
subset of their categorical wide pushout meets only finitely many factors
away from the common point. The support API characterizes coverings by the
common point plus factor ranges; every continuous map from a compact domain,
including a path, has such a finite-factor covering. There is no Hausdorff,
compact-factor, countability or finite-index assumption.

headlines.title: Charts around a common subset
headlines.text:
**Charts around a common subset.**
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointChart`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/Chart.lean)
adjoins one factor to a subset containing the common point. Distinct charts
intersect in that subset, and the subset together with the charts covers the
pushout, including an empty family. Factorwise path connectedness of its
inverse images makes the common subset path connected; a chart then needs
path connectedness only of its own whole factor. An open common subset gives
open charts, with no separation assumptions.

headlines.title: Fundamental groups of factor-plus-core charts
headlines.text:
**Fundamental groups of factor-plus-core charts.**
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointChartFundamentalGroupDesc`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/FundamentalGroup.lean)
glues homomorphisms on an arbitrary path-connected open neighborhood of the
common point and its charts, assuming path connectedness of each whole
factor. Only agreement on the core is required. The inclusion-induced
core and chart restrictions characterize the result, for arbitrary target
groups in an independent universe, empty index families and coincident
charts. If each original factor's core-preimage inclusion induces the trivial
fundamental-group map, the factor inclusion-induced coproduct map `q` is split
injective. The specified splitting extends factor homomorphisms to arbitrary
independently universed monoid targets. These hypotheses alone do not imply
surjectivity of `q` or uniqueness of these extensions. Under just the path-connected
core and whole-factor hypotheses,
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointChartFundamentalGroupColimitEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/FundamentalGroupColimit.lean)
identifies the raw group colimit of the core-to-chart star with the ambient
fundamental group. Both directions preserve every core and chart inclusion
map, including for an empty index family; no core-preimage nullity is needed.
With the split-injectivity hypotheses above,
[`FundamentalGroupKernel`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/FundamentalGroupKernel.lean)
identifies the kernel of the ambient-to-original-factor-coproduct retraction
`ρ` with the ambient algebraic normal closure of `⋃ i, γᵢ(ker pᵢ)`.
Here `γᵢ` is induced by chart inclusion; `pᵢ` comes from restricting the
ambient factor collapse to that chart and then applying the inverse ULift
homeomorphism to the original factor. Consequently, `q` is surjective exactly
when `ker pᵢ ≤ ker γᵢ` for every chart. Under this condition, `q` and the specified
`ρ` form a multiplicative equivalence, and these extensions are unique
for arbitrary independently universed monoid targets. For the inclusion family
into the ambient fundamental group, this condition is also necessary for
uniqueness: when it fails, the identity and `q.comp ρ` agree on all original-factor
restrictions but differ. No simply connected core, path-connected core preimages
or chart–factor homotopy equivalences are required.
Index and space universes are independent, and an empty family retains its point
head. No vanishing of these chart defects or free-product computation from
ordinary contractibility of chosen factor neighborhoods is asserted.

headlines.title: Subfamily retractions and continuous factorization
headlines.text:
**Subfamily retractions and continuous factorization.**
[`TopCat.widePushoutPointSubfamilyRetraction`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/Subfamily.lean)
retracts onto any subfamily, with an embedding inclusion whose range includes
the common point. This inclusion is closed exactly when the chosen-point
singleton in every omitted factor is closed; retained factors need no separation
hypothesis. A continuous map factors through that inclusion exactly
when its support lies in the subfamily, without separation or compactness
assumptions. For T₁ factors, every compact-domain map factors through a finite
subfamily. The circle-bouquet application retains the endpoints of based loops,
including included positive original-circle loops.

headlines.title: Strict finite-stage factorization of compact homotopies
headlines.text:
**Strict finite-stage factorization of compact homotopies.**
[`TopCat.exists_finite_widePushout_point_subfamily_homotopyRel`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/WidePushout/SubfamilyHomotopy.lean)
factors a prescribed compact-image relative homotopy in a point-wide-pushout
of T₁ factors through a finite subfamily containing any prescribed finite
set. Recovery holds at every pair of parameters, including both endpoint
maps and arbitrary relative subsets. Compact domains suffice, without source
separation, factor compactness or countability. At a fixed subfamily,
existence of a relative or path homotopy is reflected without T₁ or compactness.
[`CircleBouquet.loop_homotopic_iff_exists_finite_subfamily`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/CircleBouquet.lean)
gives finite-stage detection for based loops in arbitrary circle bouquets;
the stronger homotopy theorem recovers a supplied based homotopy itself.

headlines.title: Arbitrary-index circle bouquets
headlines.text:
**Arbitrary-index circle bouquets.**
[`CircleBouquet.space`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/CircleBouquet.lean) is the wide
pushout of based complex circles, with a common point even for the empty
family and independent index/ambient universes. Inclusions, descent and
extensionality give its universal property; retractions detect the positive
generators as nonidentity.
[`CircleBouquet.generatorEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/CircleBouquet/FundamentalGroup.lean)
identifies its fundamental group with `FreeGroup I`, sending each free generator
to the included counterclockwise circle class. `CircleBouquet.lift` gives the
unique extension of arbitrary generator values to a homomorphism into any
group, in an independent target universe. Distinct included positive generators
do not commute. The inverse equivalence is noncomputable; no geometric
word-extraction algorithm is asserted.
The continuous map `CircleBouquet.relabel σ` realizes arbitrary relabelings,
preserving the original positive generators and commuting with `FreeGroup.map σ`.
Source and target ambient and label universes are independent, including empty
or infinite families and noninjective label maps. The universal property is
natural under precomposition by this map through `CircleBouquet.lift_comp_relabel`.
Its [topological criteria](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/CircleBouquet/Topology.lean)
characterize closed embeddings exactly by injective label maps and quotient
maps exactly by surjective label maps. Relabeling is a
[closed map exactly when every label fiber is finite](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/CircleBouquet/ClosedMap.lean);
the bouquet has the weak/final topology, not the Hawaiian-earring subspace topology.
The induced fundamental-group homomorphism is injective or surjective exactly
when the label map has the corresponding property. Its kernel is the normal
closure of the differences `positiveGenerator i * (positiveGenerator k)⁻¹`
for equal labels `σ i = σ k`, by `CircleBouquet.ker_mapOfEq_relabel`; no
surjectivity assumption is needed.

headlines.title: Diagonal equivalence for non-antipodal pairs
headlines.text:
**Diagonal equivalence for non-antipodal pairs.** In any real normed vector
space, [`Metric.Sphere.diagonalHomotopyEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/Sphere.lean)
has the diagonal as its forward map and first projection as its inverse.
Normalized affine interpolation stays in the non-antipodal-pair subspace and
fixes the diagonal. No finite-dimensionality or nonemptiness hypothesis is needed.

headlines.title: Continuous hairy-ball theorem for S²
headlines.text:
**Continuous hairy-ball theorem for S².**
[`sphere2_exists_zero_of_orthogonal_field`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/HairyBallSphere2.lean)
says every `V : C(sphere2, E3)` pointwise orthogonal to the radius has a zero.
In any real inner-product space, a nowhere-zero continuous orthogonal field
on the metric unit sphere gives an explicit identity-to-antipodal homotopy
([`TangentField`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homotopy/TangentField.lean)), without finite
dimensionality. Only the zero theorem specializes to Euclidean three-space.

headlines.title: Circle/S² homology and antipodal sign
headlines.text:
**Circle/S² homology and antipodal sign.** Ordered punctures give
`H̃₁(S¹; ℤ) ≅ ℤ` and `H̃₂(S²; ℤ) ≅ ℤ`, in the unit-sphere models in
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` and `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`
([`Circle`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/Circle.lean),
[`Sphere`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/Sphere.lean)). The circle basis is
upper minus lower; the equator coordinate is ordered `(x,y)`.
[`SphereAntipodal`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/SphereAntipodal.lean)
computes `-id` on ordinary and reduced integral `H₂`, hence multiplication
by `-1` in the fixed integer coordinate and nonhomotopy to identity.

headlines.title: Covering-space lifts of simplices
headlines.text:
**Covering-space lifts of simplices.** For a covering `p : Y ⟶ X`,
[`IsCoveringMap.singularLiftEquiv`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Topology/SingularLifts.lean)
identifies the lift fiber of a singular simplex with a point fiber by
evaluation at any point. Restriction is bijective for every simplex
operator, including degeneracies and faces omitting vertex zero. There are
no nonemptiness, connectedness, local connectedness, surjectivity or finite-
sheet assumptions on the base or total space. The singular map is equifibered.

headlines.title: Finite-fiber covering transfer
headlines.text:
**Finite-fiber covering transfer.** For `p : Y ⟶ X`, `IsCoveringMap p` and
finite point fibers,
[`singularChainComplexTransfer`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/Transfer.lean)
uses coefficient objects in any preadditive category with coproducts indexed
in the space universe; object and morphism universes are independent.
Ordinary homology adds only `CategoryWithHomology` and uses `q : ℕ`.
A simplex maps to the sum of its lifts. Transfer then pushforward is
`d • id` if every point fiber has cardinality `d`; finiteness is a separate
premise. No constant degree, nonemptiness, surjectivity or connectedness is
needed for the construction.

headlines.title: Subdivision and cover-small chains
headlines.text:
**Subdivision and cover-small chains.** Integral signed subdivision `Sd`
and its support-preserving prism `H` satisfy `∂H + H∂ = id − Sd`
([`Subdivision`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/Subdivision.lean)). For an
open cover, inclusion of finite-support chains small in a cover member is a
quasi-isomorphism
([`SmallChains`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/SmallChains.lean)). Space
and cover-index universes may differ; no global nonemptiness is assumed.
Cover-respecting continuous maps and refinements induce compatible chain maps.

headlines.title: Ordered ordinary and reduced Mayer–Vietoris
headlines.text:
**Ordered ordinary and reduced Mayer–Vietoris.** Two opens covering a space
give difference `(c,−c)` followed by sum, all three successive ordinary
exactness positions, ordered-cover naturality and cover-swap minus sign
([`MayerVietoris`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/MayerVietoris.lean)).
The reduced low-degree boundary uses open-intersection homology and is an
isomorphism when both `H̃₀` and `H̃₁` vanish on each open. The reduced
degree-zero sequence is exact at the biproduct for every two-open cover;
its final map is epic when the intersection is nonempty, not unconditionally
([`ReducedMayerVietoris`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/ReducedMayerVietoris.lean)).

headlines.title: Components and path connectedness
headlines.text:
**Components and path connectedness.**
[`Components`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/Components.lean) presents the
augmentation kernel by nonbasepoint path components, with categorical
coefficients. In a preadditive category with the requisite coproducts and
homology, `H₀(X; R) ⟶ R` is invertible exactly when `X` is path connected
if `R` is nonzero; nonemptiness is a conclusion
([`Connectedness`](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/SphereTopology/Homology/Singular/Connectedness.lean)).
For nonempty `X`, integral `H̃₀(X)=0` is equivalent to path connectedness.
Reduced homology is nonnegative, with augmentation kernel in degree zero,
ordinary homology in positive degrees and `H̃₀(∅)=0`; no degree-minus-one
convention is asserted. Contractible-space premises include nonemptiness.

headlines.title: Covering foundations from Fundamental Groupoids
headlines.text:
**Covering foundations from Fundamental Groupoids.** The dependency supplies
based unique lifting, monodromy, maps of covers, deck actions and based
equal-image equivalences; Sphere re-exports the five deprecated covering
module paths below. The [guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sphere-topology/blob/672d46f90cf51cdf3f933248b85c842990ead729/docs/guide.md#headline-results) gives the
distinct connectedness and local path connectedness hypotheses for each
result. These are not a general classification of coverings.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.id_not_nullhomotopic_two
main_results.note: The identity of Metric.Sphere.basedSpace 1, the unit two-sphere in EuclideanSpace real (Fin 3) lifted to any universe, is not homotopic to any constant map, without a basedness restriction on the homotopy.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.homotopyQuotient_id_ne_const_two
main_results.note: The quotient classes of the identity and the constant endomorphism at the last-axis north pole of Metric.Sphere.basedSpace 1 are distinct in the based-homotopy category.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.nontrivial_sphere_two
main_results.note: The existing homotopy group on Fin 2 of Metric.Sphere.basedSpace 1 at its last-axis north pole is nontrivial in every universe. This is a named theorem, not a global instance or a computation of the group.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.cogroup_isCommMonObj_iff
main_results.note: For every n >= 0 in any universe, the specified sphere cogroup of dimension n + 1 satisfies IsCommMonObj exactly when 0 < n. Its multiplication is the original ordered-pinch class; this is a named property, not a global instance.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.cogroup_not_isCommMonObj_zero
main_results.note: The specified cogroup of the original circle S1 is not commutative, in every universe, as detected by the positive generators of Sphere's original two-circle bouquet through the sphere-map and first-homotopy-group comparisons.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.cogroup_isCommMonObj
main_results.note: In sphere dimensions n + 2 >= 2, the specified monoid object underlying the metric sphere cogroup satisfies Mathlib's IsCommMonObj; its multiplication remains the original ordered-pinch class. This is a named property, not a global instance.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.mulOppositeEquivSphereHom
main_results.note: For every n >= 0 and arbitrary X : BasedTopCat in universe u, the multiplicative opposite of the homotopy group on Fin (n + 1) is multiplicatively equivalent to the canonical group-valued Yoneda evaluation of Metric.Sphere.cogroup n; its elements unop to outgoing sphere-map classes.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.mulOppositeEquivSphereHom_apply_op
main_results.note: The forward characteristic sends MulOpposite.op a to (HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom (n + 1) X a).op, without inversion or a change of representative.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.mulOppositeEquivSphereHom_symm_apply
main_results.note: The inverse characteristic sends every incoming morphism f to MulOpposite.op ((HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom (n + 1) X).symm f.unop).

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.mulOppositeEquivSphereHom_naturality
main_results.note: Based postcomposition by h : X to Y agrees with the group-valued Yoneda action on (Q.map h).op.op, where Q is BasedTopCat.homotopyQuotient.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.cogroup
main_results.note: The lifted original positive-dimensional sphere, based at its last-axis north pole, is a stock group object in the ordinary opposite based-homotopy category; its fields are opposite to the classes of pinch, collapse and first-coordinate reflection.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.cogroupGrpObj
main_results.note: Named group-object data, with no global instance; local installation gives the stock group on outgoing based homotopy classes into any based target.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.pinchToWedge_comp_apply
main_results.note: Postcomposing the pointed pinch with an arbitrary map from the binary wedge evaluates by the original ordered fold of its two inclusion restrictions.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom
main_results.note: For every n >= 0 and arbitrary X : BasedTopCat in universe u, finite-cube homotopy classes on Fin n are equivalent as sets to based-homotopy-category morphisms from the north-based ULift of the unit n-sphere to X.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom_class
main_results.note: The forward image of a Fin n cube representative is the class of GenLoop.sphereHomeomorph n precomposed with ULift.down, including n = 0.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom_symm_map
main_results.note: The inverse image of a based unit n-sphere map class is its sphere representative precomposed with ULift.up and then pulled back along Cube.collapseToSphere n, including dimension zero.

main_results.name: HomotopyGroup.equivSphereHom_symm_map_eq_class
main_results.note: Any Fin n generalized loop with values t ↦ f.right.hom (ULift.up (Cube.collapseToSphere n t)) represents the inverse image of the class of the based sphere map f.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.pinch_comp_collapseToSphere
main_results.note: The positive-dimensional sphere pinch pulls back to coordinate-zero concatenation of the two original collapse-inclusion loops.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.pinch_nondegenerate
main_results.note: Fixed quarter and three-quarter cube witnesses map to distinct non-head values in the two original sphere factors.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.pinch_fold_class
main_results.note: Folding based maps F then G corresponds to J(G) * J(F) under the inverse sphere-class comparison and the existing multiplication, including dimension one.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.pinch_retraction_homotopicRel
main_results.note: Both original factor retractions composed with the positive-dimensional sphere pinch are homotopic to the identity relative to the last-axis north pole.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.pinch_fold_homotopicRel_swap
main_results.note: In sphere dimensions n + 2, folding arbitrary based maps in either order after the original pinch gives maps homotopic relative to the specified north pole; targets need only a topology in an independent universe.

main_results.name: Metric.Sphere.pinch_homotopicRel_swap
main_results.note: In sphere dimensions n + 2, the original categorical factor swap after the pinch is homotopic to the pinch relative to the last-axis north pole.

main_results.name: CircleBouquet.generatorMap_bijective
main_results.note: The included counterclockwise circle classes freely generate the fundamental group of an arbitrary-index circle bouquet, including an empty family.

main_results.name: CircleBouquet.generatorEquiv
main_results.note: A multiplicative equivalence from FreeGroup I to the bouquet fundamental group whose forward homomorphism is the prescribed generator map.

main_results.name: CircleBouquet.lift
main_results.note: Arbitrary generator values extend uniquely to homomorphisms into a group in an independent universe; this is not arbitrary extension into monoids.

main_results.name: CircleBouquet.positiveGenerator_mul_ne_mul
main_results.note: Positive classes from distinct included circles do not commute.

main_results.name: Complex.exists_fixedPoint_closedBall_of_boundary_mapsTo
main_results.note: A complex-valued continuous map on a closed ball with arbitrary center and nonnegative radius has a fixed point if its sphere-boundary images lie in that ball; no interior image bound or extension to the plane is assumed.

main_results.name: Complex.exists_fixedPoint_closedBall
main_results.note: Every continuous self-map of a complex closed ball with arbitrary center and nonnegative radius has a fixed point in that same ball, including the radius-zero case.

main_results.name: Circle.degree_comp_closedBall_inclusion
main_results.note: Every continuous map from the complex closed unit disk to Circle has degree-zero boundary restriction along the stock sphere-to-closed-ball inclusion, without a basedness premise.

main_results.name: Circle.comp_closedBall_inclusion_ne_id
main_results.note: The same boundary restriction is not the identity of Circle; this is the complex unit-disk non-retraction theorem.

main_results.name: TopCat.widePushoutPointRetraction_jointly_injective
main_results.note: The selected-factor retractions jointly distinguish points of an arbitrary chosen-point wide pushout, including the empty family, without separation or finiteness assumptions.

main_results.name: TopCat.t0Space_widePushoutPoint_iff
main_results.note: A chosen-point wide pushout is T0 exactly when every factor is T0, with no separation premise on either side.

main_results.name: TopCat.t1Space_widePushoutPoint_iff
main_results.note: A chosen-point wide pushout is T1 exactly when every factor is T1, with no separation premise on either side.

main_results.name: TopCat.t2Space_widePushoutPoint_iff
main_results.note: A chosen-point wide pushout is Hausdorff exactly when every factor is Hausdorff, with no separation premise on either side.

main_results.name: IsCoveringMap.singularChainComplexTransfer
main_results.note: All-simplex singular chain transfer for a covering map with finite point fibers, with a coefficient object in a preadditive category with the requisite coproducts.

main_results.name: IsCoveringMap.summandι_singularChainComplexTransfer_f
main_results.note: The characteristic formula specifies a singular simplex's image as the sum of all its lifts.

main_results.name: TopCat.isZero_reducedSingularHomologyZero_iff_pathConnectedSpace
